notes: SHIP v1.14.443 - R2 GATE A: THE CABINET GETS ITS DEPTH BACK. ONE CONSTANT MOVED. RD 4.5 to 9.0 against RW 6.0 - the cabinet was three quarters as deep as it was wide, and a real 600mm rack is 1000 to 1200mm deep, half again to twice its width. That single wrong number is the root of the directive's own complaint that the rack reads as a stack of dark rectangles: from any angle showing its side it was a shallow display case, not a cabinet. 9.0 is 1.5x width - clearly physical, deliberately short of the literal 1.78x so a first pass cannot overshoot on a phone-sized preview, and trivially tunable at R7/R8 against screenshots. WHY ONE CONSTANT IS THE WHOLE SHIP. RD is fully parametric. Corner posts, top and bottom cross-members, front AND rear rails, back wall, side panels, feet, the CDU cartridge, bus bars, both manifolds, the vertical pipes, the cable arm and the rear door all derive from it, and chassis depth is RD minus 0.42 - so the trays deepen WITH the cabinet. That is exactly section 10, chassis extends backward, servers live inside the rack. It is NOT a device-family change: no face, colour, material, LED or family treatment was touched. That is R3. CAMERA CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. fitDist is max(fitDistH, RD * 0.65) * 1.3. For 48U, fitDistH is 32.7 against RD*0.65 of 5.85 - the height term still wins by more than five times, so the JOHN-LOCKED FOV-28 ISO framing does not move. RD only becomes the driver on a very short rack, which is correct behaviour for a deep low cabinet. ZERO PERFORMANCE COST, MEASURED. Draw calls 276, triangles 6904, geometries 236, textures 4 - identical to the R1 baseline before and after, because a dimension constant adds no objects. THE REST OF R2 WAS ALREADY BUILT, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. Section 42's R2 list is cabinet proportions, frame, rails, RU mapping visibility, depth and floor contact. Read against live code: the frame already has four corner posts plus top and bottom cross-members at 1 percent of rack height, narrow, with no oversized bezel. The rails already exist as four EIA-310 perforated rails carrying three square holes per U from ONE shared CanvasTexture with repeat.y set to totalU, so the hole pitch lands on real U boundaries - added at v1.14.260 and better than the mockup, which has no holes at all. RU ticks already run every 5U on both front rails. Section 8 says improve existing rails rather than add parallel geometry; there was nothing to improve. Proportions are already sound: RW to RH is 0.368 for 48U, sitting between the mockup's 0.41 and a real cabinet's 0.28. THE FLOOR MUST NOT BE TOUCHED, AND THIS CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER NOTE. After the mockup arrived I recorded that PHANTOM should adopt its blurred contact shadow. Reading the code says the opposite. dct-ios.html carries an explicit ruling: the floor is a MeshBasicMaterial taking NO direct light, NO env and NO shadow, and receiveShadow was REMOVED to fix a defect - a specular pool that swept as you orbited, tinted mint by rimL, with the rack's own shadow cutting a dark wedge out of it. Owner's law quoted in the source: the floor only ever REFLECTS. Adding a contact shadow would revert that fix. PHANTOM already answers believable floor contact its own ruled way, through the wet reflection clone whose contact-sharp falloff IS the contact cue. The floor is done; section 26 must not be actioned. The R1 baseline note has been corrected rather than left to mislead a future session. RUNS (phone-webkit): 02-build-forge alone = 14 passed, including the x10 aisle round trip. 08-forge-layout alone = 17 passed. 29 + 30 + 24 + 23 + 22 + 20 = 37 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .443. NO device family, material, light, fog, tone-mapping, colour or floor change. DEVICE-VERIFY, one look: open BUILD with an active rack and look at the preview. PASS is a cabinet that reads as a box with real depth - a visible side wall receding, a top surface, trays set back inside it. FAIL is a flat frame, a rack that no longer fits the preview area, or any change to the colour of the devices.
